answer_verbatim:
If you want the **best online courses** for shadow work and spiritual practice, the strongest options from the results are **Jung Platform’s “Introduction to Jungian Shadow Work,” ManTalks’ “Shadow Course,”** and **Awake Academy’s “Embracing the Shadow”** because they are explicitly centered on shadow integration and guided inner work.[2][15][16]

A practical short list:

- **Introduction to Jungian Shadow Work (Jung Platform)** — a strong pick if you want a more psychologically grounded approach, with guidance from James Hollis and an emphasis on recognizing repeated patterns and counterproductive behaviors.[2]
- **Shadow Course: Discover Your Hidden Potential (ManTalks)** — an 8-week guided process for facing and integrating the shadow; good if you want a structured program rather than a short primer.[15]
- **Embracing The Shadow (Awake Academy / Charlie Morley)** — positioned as a transformative shadow-work course and likely appealing if you want a spiritual-development framing alongside inner healing.[16]
- **Shadow Work Course and Workbook (Udemy)** — includes lessons, exercises, diagrams, quotes, meditations, prayers, and practices, so it is one of the more explicitly *spiritual-practice-friendly* options in the results.[10]
- **Inner Healing Shadow Work Course (Sacred Humans Co.)** — described as comprehensive and covering emotional regulation, spiritual awakening, relationships, and mindful living, which makes it a broad fit for combined shadow work and spiritual practice.[14]
- **Shadow Work: Heal & Integrate your Shadow Self (Udemy)** — a more accessible option if you want a general introduction with a spiritual-growth angle.[3]

If you want the best fit by goal:

- **Most Jungian / psychologically oriented:** Jung Platform.[2]
- **Most structured guided journey:** ManTalks Shadow Course.[15]
- **Most explicitly spiritual:** Udemy’s Shadow Work Course and Workbook, and Sacred Humans Co.[10][14]
- **Most beginner-friendly / budget-conscious:** Udemy courses are usually the easiest place to start because they are typically self-paced and lower-cost than coaching-style programs.[3][10][12][13]

For a balanced practice, the course result plus the general shadow-work guidance suggests the most effective programs are the ones that combine **reflection, journaling, emotional inquiry, meditation, and pattern observation**, rather than only theory.[19][2][10]
